bihar_raw_news.title: RVNL wins ₹903 crore order from SJVN Thermal for Buxar thermal power project
bihar_raw_news.content: RVNL wins ₹903 crore order from SJVN Thermal for Buxar thermal power project Shares of Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd ended at ₹212.00, up by ₹2.50, or 1.19%, on the BSE. By Jomy Jos Pullokaran September 4, 2026, 8:16:03 PM IST (Published) 2 Min Read Navratna public sector undertaking Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd on Friday (September 4) said it has received a ₹903 crore Letter of Award from SJVN Thermal Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Limited, for work related to the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project in Bihar. The order is valued at ₹903 crore, including Goods and Services Tax (GST). Under the contract, RVNL will construct a permanent siding along with an aerial connection via track from the plant boundary to Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur at Buxar, as part of Phase III of the project. The order has been awarded by a domestic entity and is in the normal course of RVNL’s business. The execution period is 36 months. RVNL said the promoter, promoter group and group companies have no interest in SJVN Thermal Private Limited. The order also does not fall under related-party transactions. ALSO READ | RVNL partners with Goa government to develop infrastructure projects in the state Yesterday, Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd has emerged as the lowest bidder for a ₹404.88-crore project from East Coast Railway, the state-owned company said in an exchange filing. The project involves a range of civil and railway infrastructure works, including construction of the roadbed and bridges, track laying, supply of ballast, buildings and road underbridges. RVNL will also undertake utility shifting, signalling and telecommunications work, electrification, power-supply arrangements and the shifting or modification of high- and low-tension electricity lines. The ₹404.88-crore contract value includes GST. ALSO READ | RVNL shares gain after winning ₹161 crore order from East Coast Railway The work is connected to the construction of a third railway line on the Nergundi-Barang and Khurda Road-Vizianagaram stretches. Together, the two stretches cover 385 km — 22 km between Nergundi and Barang and 363 km between Khurda Road and Vizianagaram. Adding a third line can increase a railway corridor's capacity by allowing it to handle more passenger and freight trains and reducing congestion on existing tracks. RVNL has emerged as the L1, or lowest, bidder for the project. Being L1 typically puts the company in pole position for the contract, but it isn't the same as receiving the final Letter of Acceptance. Shares of Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd ended at ₹212.00, up by ₹2.50, or 1.19%, on the BSE. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Promotes Aquaculture Insurance Under PM-MKSSY - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Promotes Aquaculture Insurance Under PM-MKSSY 04 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar is promoting aquaculture insurance for fish farmers under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) , providing financial support on insurance premiums and additional benefits for SC, ST and women fish farmers . Key Points Insurance Support: Fish farmers can receive a 40% one-time incentive on insurance premiums , up to ₹1 lakh . SC, ST and women beneficiaries can receive an additional 10% incentive , taking the maximum benefit to ₹1.10 lakh . Insurance Coverage: Insurance coverage can extend up to ₹20 lakh , depending on the premium paid. Eligible Area: For the one-time incentive, eligible water-spread area is calculated at ₹25,000 per hectare , with a maximum limit of 4 hectares . The scheme covers ponds, aquaculture farms, RAS, cages, bio-floc and raceway systems. Covers risks such as floods, cyclones, pollution, drought and other natural disasters. Bihar’s Fish Production: Fish production increased from 9.69 lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25 to 10.28 lakh metric tonnes in 2025-26 . The state has 233 fish seed hatcheries , meeting around 70% of its fish seed requirement . Bihar has 89 fish feed mills , producing around 50,000 tonnes of fish feed locally . Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY): Nature: Implemented as a Central Sector Sub-scheme under the Central Sector Component of PMMSY . Outlay: ₹6,000 crore. Public Finance: ₹3,000 crore (50%) , including World Bank and AFD external financing . Beneficiary/Private Investment: ₹3,000 crore (50%) through anticipated beneficiary and private-sector investment. Duration: 4 years , from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 . Today it has 39 times. Bihar has just committed ₹1.38 lakh crore to close it with a run to 24 GW, even as Karnataka plots a run to 66 GW of its own. Chitrika Grover 04 Sep 2026 14:18 IST Follow Us A decade ago, Karnataka had 29 times Bihar's renewable capacity. Today it has 39 times. That widening gap is the first half of this story. The second half is that Bihar has just committed ₹1.38 lakh crore to close it with a run to 24 GW, even as Karnataka plots a run to 66 GW of its own. Advertisment Karnataka spent the last decade turning an early lead into outright dominance. Bihar spent it almost entirely on the sidelines, and is only now, in the last two years, showing the first real signs of a state that intends to catch up. bihar_raw_news.title: India's scheme for rare earth magnet production gains broad industry participation: Report
bihar_raw_news.content: International 03 Sep, 2026 India's scheme for rare earth magnet production gains broad industry participation: Report Business To Business, New Delhi, 03 September 2026: India has received 20 bids to build integrated rare‑earth permanent magnet manufacturing facilities and the government aims to create an integrated chain stretching from NdPr oxide to finished magnets, a new report has said. The report from Times Kuwait highlighted that India’s broader critical-mineral strategy increasingly focuses on value addition, processing and manufacturing rather than stopping at the extraction stage. The warm response by bidders to the initiative has given fresh momentum to a policy effort that goes beyond securing a raw material to forming industrial capacity necessary to convert India’s rare-earth resources into high-value products for the country's fastest-growing sector, the report said. India's $7.74 billion rare‑earth permanent scheme aims to create 6,000 metric tonnes per annum of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity in India. Ministry of Heavy Industries invited proposals on March 20, 2026 and opened technical bids on August 13, 2026, as companies including Larsen & Toubro, Coal India, ReNew, Attero Recycling, 20 Microns, Lohum Magnets & Energy Solutions, NEO Performance Materials of Singapore and Proterial India responded. “Twenty companies and consortia submitted bids, bringing together established engineering companies, public-sector enterprises, recycling specialists, energy companies, magnet manufacturers and international participants,” the publication said. The scheme targets up to five beneficiaries, selected through global competitive bidding, each eligible for as much as 1,200 metric tonnes per annum. The scheme design places production at the centre of the programme, the report said, adding that it connects government support to the actual manufacture and sale of magnets rather than focusing solely on creating facilities. The publication mentioned broad participation of firms from different industrial backgrounds as evidence of rare-earth processing and magnet manufacturing being viewed as a wider industrial opportunity. India’s policy emphasis is now shifting towards connecting substantial rare-earth resources with industrial value chains. Government assessments indicated a huge gap between upstream capabilities and industrial-scale midstream and downstream manufacturing. The timing of the rare-earth push is also closely connected to India’s broader technology and manufacturing ambitions along with advances in mobile phones and electronics exports, Permanent magnets sit at the intersection of many of these sectors including semiconductors, electric mobility, renewable energy equipment and advanced manufacturing. bihar_raw_news.title: Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP over youth protests | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 03, 2026 Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP against suppressing voice of youth Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi interacts with students from Bihar injured during protests against alleged irregularities in examination system, at his residence, in New Delhi. (@RahulGandhi/X via PTI Photo) Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday backed students and youngsters in Bihar who protested against alleged irregularities in the examination system, and warned the BJP that any government that suppresses the voice of the youth will eventually have to answer to the people. Gandhi made the remarks after meeting students and young people who, he said, had faced “horrific police brutality” while raising their concerns over the examination system. “Police lathis as well as gunfire from AK-47 and pistols left many students injured. A young man aspiring to serve the country in the Army had his leg battered by an AK-47 bullet -- and with it, his life-long dream was also shattered,” Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. He said the protesters were only demanding fair opportunities, a transparent examination system and their rights. “What was the need to use lathis and bullets in response to such demands?” Gandhi asked. He also rejected any attempt to hold only lower-ranking officials responsible for the police action. “The government cannot absolve itself of responsibility for such extreme brutality by merely blaming a few low-ranking officials. This action is either the result of orders from above or a sign of the administration's utter failure,” he said. Gandhi said he stood with the protesting youngsters and was ready to provide them with all possible assistance. “The BJP should remember: any regime that suppresses the voice of the youth eventually has to answer to the people. That day is not far off,” he said. Patna witnessed clashes between job aspirants and police last month after protesters tried to march towards the chief minister’s residence, demanding a single-tier teacher recruitment examination and a transparent recruitment process. The students’ agitation, which began in the first week of August, has received support from opposition leaders, including RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: How a 57-YO Barrage Helped Shield Bihar From the Nepal Himalayan Flood Surge
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Sustainability How a 57-YO Barrage Helped Shield Bihar From the Nepal Himalayan Flood Surge How a 57-YO Barrage Helped Shield Bihar From the Nepal Himalayan Flood Surge As floodwaters from Nepal surged towards Bihar, engineers opened all 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. By TBI Team 04 Sep 2026 As floodwaters from Nepal surged towards Bihar, engineers opened all 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. By TBI Team 04 Sep 2026 Follow Us New Update As the flood surge intensified, engineers opened all 36 gates of the barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. On 26 August, catastrophic floods swept through parts of Nepal, leaving hundreds dead and thousands missing as swollen rivers tore through communities. Advertisment The floodwaters surged through the Trishuli and Narayani river systems before entering India as the Gandak. As the Himalayan disaster moved towards Bihar, the state faced the threat of a massive influx of water. Advertisment Add The Better India As A Trusted Source At Valmikinagar, however, engineers had a crucial piece of infrastructure on their side: the 57-year-old Gandak Barrage. As the flood surge intensified, engineers opened all 36 gates of the barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. The aim was to manage the enormous volume of water flowing downstream and prevent an even more destructive surge from overwhelming the region. The intervention did come at a cost. Low-lying areas of West Champaran were flooded, agricultural fields went underwater , and families had to be evacuated from vulnerable areas. But the barrage helped regulate the incoming water at a critical moment, potentially reducing the impact of the Himalayan flood surge on downstream communities. View this post on Instagram Without such regulation, an unchecked surge could have inundated larger stretches of Bihar, damaged vast areas of farmland and deposited huge quantities of Himalayan silt across the plains. Communities in vulnerable areas would also have had far less time to respond. Built to manage the worst The Gandak Barrage was constructed as part of the 1959 Gandak Agreement between India and Nepal, with the broader Gandak river system being developed to regulate water and support irrigation across the region. Located at Valmikinagar in West Champaran, the barrage has spent decades controlling the flow of one of the major rivers entering Bihar from the Himalayan region. Its importance becomes particularly evident during extreme weather events, when enormous volumes of water can move rapidly from the mountains into the plains. More than half a century after it was built , the barrage once again became a critical line of defence when a Himalayan flood disaster reached India's doorstep. For the communities downstream, it was a reminder that infrastructure built decades ago can play a crucial role when nature unleashes its most powerful forces. bihar_raw_news.title: Foodgrain production estimated at 376.5 million tonnes amid robust decentralised grain storage infra
bihar_raw_news.content: Business 03 Sep, 2026 Foodgrain production estimated at 376.5 million tonnes amid robust decentralised grain storage infra Business To Business, New Delhi, 03 September 2026: The country’s total foodgrain production is estimated at 376.563 million tonnes, according to the Third Advance Estimates (2025-26), which is nearly 18.8 million tonnes (5.3 per cent) higher than last year’s production of 357.732 million tonnes, an official factsheet said on Thursday. India also operates one of the world’s largest food security programmes under the National Food Security Act, 2013, that covers about 80 crore people. “India’s expanding agricultural production and food security efforts have increased the importance of decentralised grain storage infrastructure across the country. The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, launched in 2023, is designed to improve storage, processing, procurement, and distribution systems through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS),” the factsheet noted. The plan is supported through institutional coordination and financial support mechanisms. Beginning with pilot projects across 11 states/PACS with 9,750 MT of storage capacity, the initiative has expanded steadily. As of July 2026, godown construction had been completed in 313 PACS across the country, creating more than 1.80 LMT of storage capacity. The framework also emphasises quality standards, transparency and operational viability, according to the factsheet. The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector seeks to reduce foodgrain wastage and strengthen food security; provide farmers with greater flexibility to avoid distress sales and secure better price realization; reduce transportation costs between procurement centres, warehouses, and Fair Price Shops; and expand the role of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) through diversification of agricultural activities. It also supports higher income opportunities for farmers. The pilot projects were implemented in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Assam, Karnataka, and Tripura. These pilots have provided an important operational foundation and demonstrated the feasibility of local storage infrastructure at the cooperative level, said the factsheet. According to the official statement, the Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector represents an integrated approach towards improving agricultural infrastructure through cooperatives. By linking storage, processing, procurement, and distribution at the PACS level, the Plan strengthens foodgrain management closer to production centres. national_raw_news.title: 6 mins ago | National 248 Janmashtami being celebrated across the country today
national_raw_news.content: The festival of Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna, is being celebrated across the country with religious fervour today. On the occasion, devotees observe fasts, perform ceremonies and visit temples. Sweets and other foods associated with Krishna are prepared and offered to Lord Krishna. Devotional songs and chanting are performed throughout the day and often late into the night. Temples and homes have been decorated with scenes depicting episodes from Krishna’s life, such as his childhood in Gokul and Vrindavan. Akashvani Uttar Pradesh Correspondent reports that the city of Lord Krishna, Mathura-Vrindavan, is decked up for the grand celebration tonight. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will take part in Janmashtami celebrations in Mathura today. In view of the huge crowd of devotees coming from across the country and abroad, extensive security arrangements have been made in the city. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to citizens on Janmashtami. In her message, the President said the life and teachings of Lord Krishna breathe new life into India’s cultural and philosophical heritage. She said Lord Krishna’s teachings, embodied in the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, remain an eternal source of inspiration for humanity to make prudent decisions during difficult times and remain steadfast in moral values. The President said Janmashtami inspires everyone to uphold the spirit of harmony and devotion to duty and service. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to the people on Janmashtami. He said devotion and love for Lord Shri Krishna are boundless among his countless devotees in India and across the world. Mr Birla said the profound wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita offers timeless guidance on duty, ethics, justice, wisdom, courage and balance in life.
